variations.name: CO2 mineral curing/injection in ready-mix and precast concrete
variations.description: Liquid CO2 is injected into fresh ready-mix or used to cure precast elements, where it mineralizes into calcium carbonate that permanently stores the CO2 while letting producers cut cement content at little or no extra cost — the lowest-friction retrofit path to storing CO2 in mainstream concrete.

companies.name: CarbonCure Technologies
companies.what: Retrofits ready-mix and masonry plants with CO2 injection systems and monetizes the stored CO2 through a shared-revenue carbon credit program.
companies.signal: $169M raised (Amazon, Microsoft, Breakthrough Energy, Blue Earth); 10 million truckloads and ~690,000 t CO2 milestone announced Nov 2025; systems in 25+ countries.

companies.name: Solidia Technologies
companies.what: Pioneered CO2-cured calcium-silicate precast concrete and has pivoted to licensing its 300+ patent portfolio plus selling a CO2-mineralizing SCM (35-50% cement replacement).
companies.signal: Licensed low-carbon cement IP and sold plant/lab assets to CalPortland (Jun 2024); completed 25 pilot projects in 2024; San Antonio HQ pilot SCM line commissioned 2023.

companies.name: Carbonaide
companies.what: VTT spinout selling automated production-scale CO2-curing lines for precast concrete factories, halving cement content while mineralizing CO2.
companies.signal: Commercial production in Finland since early 2024; global rollout partnership with precast machinery maker Elematic (May 2025); €1.8M seed (2023) plus €3.7M round (Jan 2026).

companies.name: Kajima Corporation (CO2-SUICOM consortium)
companies.what: Japanese construction giant that co-developed CO2-SUICOM carbon-negative concrete (with Chugoku Electric, Denka, Landes), replacing over half the cement with a CO2-hardening admixture.
companies.signal: CUCO-SUICOM blocks and shotcrete deployed at Expo 2025 Osaka (~3,300 m2 of paving fixing ~9.7 t CO2); joint DAC-to-concrete program with Kawasaki Heavy Industries.

variations.name: Carbonation of recycled concrete and demolition fines
variations.description: Crushed demolition concrete and cement-paste fines are exposed to concentrated CO2, which reacts with the hydrated cement to re-form limestone — turning construction waste into a permanent CO2 sink and an improved aggregate or clinker substitute.

companies.name: neustark
companies.what: Builds modular carbonation units at concrete-recycling yards that inject biogas-sourced CO2 into demolition granulate, selling the result as certified carbon removal.
companies.signal: ~30 sites operating across Europe by mid-2025 with ~40 more in pipeline; first UK site with Aggregate Industries; Holcim strategic partnership (2023); ~$69M growth round led by Decarbonization Partners (BlackRock/Temasek).

companies.name: Heidelberg Materials
companies.what: Runs the ReConcrete process that separates recycled concrete paste and force-carbonates it into an SCM-like material for new composite cements.
companies.signal: Launched its first industrial-scale enforced-carbonation facility in Poland (Jul 2025); ReConcrete is core to its circularity/CCU roadmap.

companies.name: Holcim
companies.what: World's largest cement/aggregates group rolling out neustark carbonation across its own concrete-recycling network and backing CO2-to-materials startups via Maqer Ventures.
companies.signal: Strategic investment and collaboration agreement with neustark (2023); Maqer Ventures is an investor in Paebbl.

companies.name: Sika
companies.what: Developed the reCO2ver concrete-recycling process that breaks old concrete back into aggregate, sand and binder while injecting CO2 into the recovered fines.
companies.signal: Patented process demonstrated at pilot scale; backed by one of the world's largest admixture businesses.

companies.name: Zirkulit AG
companies.what: Eberhard Group venture selling 'zirkulit' circular concrete made with maximized recycled content plus an integrated CO2-storage step in the recycled granulate.
companies.signal: Commercially available in the Zurich region since 2021 as the first circular concrete with CO2 storage; built on Eberhard's demolition-recycling operations.

variations.name: Synthetic aggregates from carbonated industrial residues
variations.description: Alkaline industrial wastes — air-pollution-control residues, slags and ashes — are reacted with CO2 to form carbonate-bonded pellets that replace quarried aggregate, earning revenue twice: from waste-disposal gate fees and from carbon-negative product sales.

companies.name: O.C.O Technology
companies.what: Operates three UK plants using Accelerated Carbonation Technology to convert hazardous energy-from-waste APC residues into M-LS carbon-negative lightweight aggregate.
companies.signal: ~350,000 t/yr aggregate produced, treating ~25% of UK APCr; JV with Petronor for a Bilbao facility; Japan partnership with Kobelco Eco-Solutions showcased at Expo 2025 Osaka.

companies.name: Carbon8 Systems
companies.what: Licensed modular CO2ntainer units for on-site carbonation of cement bypass dust, steel and EfW residues into CircaBuild aggregate (a Greenwich University spinout, distinct from O.C.O).
companies.signal: Raised £5M from EDF and Vicat (2022) and won the Queen's Award (2017), but entered administration 12 Nov 2025 after failing to secure new funding; operations closed, 11 staff made redundant.

companies.name: Blue Planet Systems
companies.what: Geomimetic process coats particles with synthetic limestone made from dissolved CO2 and waste alkalinity (including returned concrete) to make coarse aggregate that is ~44% by mass permanently stored CO2.
companies.signal: Placed world's first net-zero embodied-carbon concrete slab with 75% synthetic aggregate (Feb 2025); expanding Pittsburg, CA plant toward ~10,000 t CO2/yr; backers include Chevron and Mitsubishi.

companies.name: MCi Carbon
companies.what: Australian mineral-carbonation platform converting industrial CO2 plus minerals/slags into calcium and magnesium carbonates and silica for construction materials.
companies.signal: 'Myrtle' demonstration plant at Orica's Kooragang Island site launched in 2025 (showcased at COP30), converting ~1,000 t CO2/yr into ~10,000 t of materials; AU$14.6M federal CCUS grant.

variations.white_space: Economics hinge on being paid to take hazardous waste (gate fees) plus carbon revenue — Carbon8's collapse shows equipment-licensing without owning the waste relationship struggles; the opening is operator models co-located at EfW/steel sites outside the UK, where regulation still sends most APC residue to landfill.

variations.name: Cement-free slag- and lime-based blocks cured with CO2
variations.description: Concrete masonry made with steel-slag or hydrated-lime binders instead of Portland cement gains its strength inside CO2 curing chambers, eliminating cement emissions entirely while permanently mineralizing captured CO2 in the block.

companies.name: CarbiCrete
companies.what: Licenses a process for cement-free CMUs that replace cement with ground steel slag and cure with waste CO2, giving blocks a ~20x lower footprint than industry average.
companies.signal: Producing via licensees Patio Drummond (QC) and Canal Block (ON, Oct 2025); Isobloc ZERO insulated block launched Jun 2025; POINT.P (Saint-Gobain) plant in France slated Q1 2026; $8M NGen-supported scale-up completed.

companies.name: CarbonBuilt
companies.what: UCLA spinout whose Reversa lime-based binder lets existing block plants cure with dilute CO2 (even from on-site biomass or DAC), cutting embodied carbon 70%+ at cost parity.
companies.signal: First commercial deployment at Blair Block, Alabama (2023); Meta capital partnership (Dec 2024) funding conversion of two more plants in Arizona and Alabama for data-center masonry.

companies.name: Orbix
companies.what: Belgian stainless-steel-slag processor whose patented Carbstone technology uses CO2 as the binder for slag-based blocks, industrialized with blockmaker Masterbloc.
companies.signal: Commercial Carbstone wall blocks on the Belgian market; CO2nstruct/CO2ncreat consortium (Prefer, Fluxys, Lhoist, Orbix) won €4.5M EU Innovation Fund grant; blocks used in BESIX/Vanhout renovation projects.

companies.name: C-Crete Technologies
companies.what: Makes pourable cement-free binders from non-carbonate feedstocks (granite, zeolite) that absorb CO2 over time, demonstrated in cast-in-place commercial pours.
companies.signal: Multiple DOE awards and real-world cement-free pours in Seattle and New York (2023-2024), including CO2-injected versions.

variations.name: Carbonated SCMs and recarbonated low-carbon cements
variations.description: CO2 is reacted with industrial byproducts, olivine, or recaptured kiln lime to produce supplementary cementitious materials and reactive carbonate cements that displace clinker — embedding captured CO2 in the binder itself rather than the aggregate.

companies.name: Fortera
companies.what: ReCarb process captures a cement kiln's own CO2 and recombines it with calcined lime into reactive vaterite 'ReAct' cement, built from the ashes of Calera's chemistry.
companies.signal: $85M Series C (Aug 2024, led by Khosla Ventures and Temasek); Redding, CA plant operating at 15,000 t/yr cement capturing 6,000 t CO2; Microsoft partnership to scale Redding toward 400,000 t/yr.

companies.name: Carbon Upcycling Technologies
companies.what: Mechanochemically reacts flue-gas CO2 with fly ash, slag and natural minerals in pressurized reactors to make enhanced SCMs that cut clinker content.
companies.signal: $34.3M (2023) and $18M (2025) raised plus $10M equipment financing; first commercial unit at CRH's Ash Grove cement plant in Mississauga targeting ~30,000 t/yr SCM from H2 2026; CRH and Cemex are partners.

companies.name: Paebbl
companies.what: Continuously carbonates ground olivine with captured CO2 in pressurized reactors to produce a carbon-storing mineral filler/SCM for concrete.
companies.signal: $25M Series A (2024; Holcim Maqer Ventures, Amazon Climate Pledge Fund); Rotterdam demo plant producing ~3 t/day from H1 2025; offtake/development collaboration with Microsoft.

companies.name: Seratech
companies.what: Imperial College spinout dissolving olivine in acid and using flue-gas CO2 to co-produce silica SCM and magnesium carbonate, enabling fully carbon-neutral concrete mixes.
companies.signal: Obel Award 2022; lab/pilot stage with first pilot facility planned and first industrial facility targeted around 2027.

variations.name: Flue-gas direct mineralization to salable minerals (sodium bicarbonate, PCC, magnesium carbonates)
variations.description: CO2 scrubbed from flue gas is reacted with brines, lime or slag-derived calcium to precipitate salable minerals such as sodium bicarbonate and precipitated calcium carbonate, using product revenue rather than carbon credits to pay for capture.

companies.name: CarbonFree
companies.what: Runs the SkyMine plant (San Antonio, since 2015) making sodium bicarbonate and chemicals from cement flue gas, and is building SkyCycle to convert steel-mill CO2 into specialty calcium carbonate.
companies.signal: Definitive agreement with U.S. Steel (Apr 2024) for a 50,000 t CO2/yr SkyCycle plant at Gary Works, Indiana — first commercial CCU plant at a North American steel mill, operations slated 2027.

companies.name: Calera
companies.what: Khosla-backed pioneer that combined power-plant flue gas with seawater/brines to make cementitious calcium carbonate and fiber-cement board.
companies.signal: Raised well over $100M and built pilot lines, but shut down its CO2-to-materials business around 2015 because the economics never worked; former employees founded Fortera (2019) on successor chemistry.

companies.name: Twence
companies.what: Dutch waste-to-energy operator running the world's first WtE flue-gas-to-sodium-bicarbonate unit, closing the loop by reusing the bicarbonate for its own flue-gas cleaning.
companies.signal: Hengelo bicarbonate unit fully operational since 2016; added a 100,000 t/yr CO2 capture/liquefaction plant for greenhouse horticulture (2023).

companies.name: Greenore
companies.what: Columbia University spinout that leaches calcium from steel slag and mineralizes dilute flue-gas CO2 at ambient conditions into carbon-negative PCC, silica and iron-oxide co-products.
companies.signal: Third Derivative portfolio company; named APAC Cleantech 25; piloting with steel-industry partners in China and the US.

companies.name: CleanO2
companies.what: Sells CarbinX micro-units that bolt onto commercial-building gas boilers and convert flue CO2 into potassium carbonate (pearl ash) sold into soaps and detergents.
companies.signal: Units deployed across Canada, the US and Japan (including 8 with Tokyo Gas); each unit captures ~6-8 t CO2/yr.

companies.name: Minerals Technologies (Specialty Minerals)
companies.what: Operates dozens of satellite PCC plants at paper mills that have for decades mineralized lime-kiln flue-gas CO2 into precipitated calcium carbonate filler — the mature commercial precedent for CO2-to-carbonate products.
companies.signal: NYSE-listed incumbent (~$2B revenue) with satellite PCC plants worldwide.

variations.white_space: Salable-mineral markets (bicarbonate, PCC) are small and price-sensitive relative to CO2 volumes — Calera proved product revenue alone rarely pays for capture; viable openings are co-location with free CO2 and free alkalinity (steel slag, WtE residue, cement CKD) or high-purity specialty grades, not commodity scale.

variations.name: CO2-absorbing cement additives and coatings
variations.description: Mineral additives mixed into fresh concrete, or lime-based coatings applied to surfaces, actively absorb and mineralize CO2 from the air or mix water over the product's life — adding carbon storage and often strength to otherwise conventional materials.

companies.name: Concrete4Change
companies.what: Nottingham startup whose CO2-saturated carrier-material additive mineralizes CO2 inside fresh concrete, boosting strength ~20% so producers can cut cement.
companies.signal: £2.5M seed (Jan 2024) led by Zacua Ventures with Goldbeck's family office; £4.5M total raised incl. grants; Series A targeted late 2025/early 2026.

companies.name: Carbon Limit
companies.what: Florida startup selling CaptureCrete, a reactive natural-mineral powder additive that makes placed concrete pull CO2 from ambient air and mineralize it.
companies.signal: $740k federal award through the South Florida ClimateReady Tech Hub (2024-2025) to scale CaptureCrete; product commercially listed for ready-mix and precast.

companies.name: Graphenstone
companies.what: Spanish manufacturer of graphene-reinforced lime paints and coatings that reabsorb CO2 as the lime carbonates during curing.
companies.signal: Sold in dozens of countries; one of the most widely distributed 'CO2-absorbing paint' brands with Cradle-to-Cradle certification.

variations.white_space: Sparse field because in-service CO2 uptake is diffusion-limited, slow, and hard to measure — MRV and prescriptive concrete codes block credit monetization; the opening is an additive with third-party-verified uptake tied to an approved carbon-credit methodology, sold through existing admixture giants (Sika, Master Builders, Mapei) rather than direct.

variations.name: Biogenic CO2 mineralization into building products (biocement/bio-concrete)
variations.description: Microalgae or bacteria biologically precipitate calcium carbonate that binds aggregate into blocks, tiles and panels, locking photosynthetically captured CO2 into masonry without Portland cement — an extension variation added for completeness.

companies.name: Prometheus Materials
companies.what: CU Boulder spinout using photosynthetic microalgae to grow a zero-carbon biocement for masonry units, pavers and acoustic panels (ProZERO).
companies.signal: Backed by Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund and Autodesk Foundation; SOM design partnership; bio-concrete supplied to the New York Climate Exchange campus project (2025).

companies.name: Biomason
companies.what: Grows Biolith tiles and precast units with carbonate-precipitating bacteria at ambient temperature, replacing fired and cement-bound products.
companies.signal: ~$36.7M Series D (Jan 2025) on top of a $65M Series C; new CEO from the cement industry after restructuring and repeated layoffs — scaling has been rocky.

companies.name: Minus Materials
companies.what: CU Boulder spinout cultivating coccolithophore microalgae to grow biogenic limestone intended as a carbon-neutral feedstock for portland cement.
companies.signal: Pre-seed/lab stage; limited public activity since 2023.

variations.white_space: Biology is slow and nutrient/bioreactor costs are high against $100/t concrete, so few players survive scale-up (see Biomason's turbulence); the near-term opening is high-margin architectural, acoustic and facade products licensed into existing precast plants rather than owned commodity production.
